# latentmixtures

A tidy R interface to the Julia package
[LatentMixtures.jl](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentmixtures-jl/):
latent class analysis (LCA), latent profile analysis (LPA), latent
transition analysis (LTA), multigroup models with full, partial or no
measurement invariance, two-level (multilevel) latent class and profile
models with cluster-level latent classes, and latent class growth /
growth mixture models (including parallel processes). It supports FIML
for missing data, sampling weights, one-step covariates, three-step
auxiliary models (R3STEP, BCH, DCAT), robust (MLR) standard errors, and
the VLMR/LMR and bootstrap likelihood-ratio tests. Random starts run on
several threads. Results agree with Mplus on the validation cases in
`tests/`.

You write R: data frames, pipes and tidyselect column choice. The
estimation runs in one persistent Julia process.

## Installation

1.  **Julia** (\>= 1.12), for example with
    [juliaup](https://github.com/JuliaLang/juliaup):

    ``` sh
    curl -fsSL https://install.julialang.org | sh
    ```

    JuliaConnectoR must be able to find `julia`. If it is not on the
    `PATH`, set `JULIA_BINDIR` (e.g. in `~/.Renviron`:
    `JULIA_BINDIR=~/.juliaup/bin`).

2.  **R packages**:

    ``` r
    install.packages(c("JuliaConnectoR", "rlang", "tidyselect", "remotes"))
    # the repository is private: set a GitHub token first, e.g. Sys.setenv(GITHUB_PAT = "...")
    remotes::install_github("williamlorder/latentmixtures")
    # or from a local checkout
    install.packages("path/to/latentmixtures", repos = NULL, type = "source")
    ```

3.  **Julia packages**: install LatentMixtures.jl into the default Julia
    environment, from GitHub (default) or from a local copy (development
    mode):

    ``` r
    latentmixtures::install_julia_packages()      # Pkg.add(url = "https://github.com/williamlorder/LatentMixtures.jl")
    # or: install_julia_packages(path = "path/to/LatentMixtures.jl")
    ```

    The repositories are private: you need read access, and Git must be
    able to authenticate to github.com (for example `gh auth login`
    followed by `gh auth setup-git`, or a personal access token in your
    Git credential helper).

Documentation:
<https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentmixtures/>.

## Quick start

The package ships five simulated datasets with known generating models
(`?aces`, `?wellbeing`, `?wellbeing_panel`, `?depression`,
`?substance`); every example below runs as is.

``` r
library(latentmixtures)
lm_available()               # TRUE once Julia and LatentMixtures.jl are installed
lm_start(threads = 4)        # optional: starts Julia once; fitting functions auto-start it

# LCA: eight adverse childhood experiences (ace_*) of 1,500 adults. Which patterns of
# childhood adversity are there? (generated with four classes)
data(aces)
m4 <- aces |> lca(starts_with("ace_"), K = 4)
convergence(m4)              # check that the best LL is replicated and EM reached the maximum
m4                           # header, fit, class sizes, item-response probabilities
summary(m4)                  # every parameter with robust standard errors
head(classify(m4))           # posterior probabilities and modal class per row

# covariates, known groups, weights: also columns of the data
lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4, covariates = c(female, low_parent_edu), weights = weight)
lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4, group = female, invariance = "ace_sex_abuse")

# LPA: sleep, activity, diet, stress, loneliness and life satisfaction
data(wellbeing)
lpa(wellbeing, sleep:lifesat, K = 4, variances = "varying")
# mixed indicator types: binary ACE items with an overdispersed symptom count (Mplus COUNT)
mixture(aces, K = 4, categorical = starts_with("ace_"), negbin = depress)
# LTA: alcohol, binge drinking, cigarettes and cannabis in grades 8, 10 and 12
data(substance)
t3 <- lta(substance, waves = list(alc_1:mj_1, alc_2:mj_2, alc_3:mj_3), K = 3)
transitions(t3)
# growth mixtures: depressive (dep1-dep5) and anxiety (anx1-anx5) symptoms, ages 12-16
data(depression)
g <- growth(depression, dep1:dep5, K = 4, model = "gmm", degree = 2)
growth(depression, processes = list(dep1:dep5, anx1:anx5), K = 4, model = "gmm")
# two-level LCA: students in schools, 3 student classes and 2 latent school types
data(schools)
ml <- lca(schools, starts_with("b_"), K = 3, level2 = school, KB = 2)
conditionalprobs(ml)         # P(student class | school type)

# three-step auxiliary models: model, data, columns
r3step(m4, aces, c(female, age, low_parent_edu), ref = 1)   # who is in which class?
bch(m4, aces, depress)       # depressive symptoms by class (generated means 4 to 13)
dcat(m4, aces, srh, ref = 1) # self-rated health by class

# class enumeration tests: 4 against 3 classes
lmr(m4); blrt(m4, reps = 100)

# nested models with the same K (e.g. measurement invariance across sex): naive and
# Satorra-Bentler scaled (MLR) difference tests, as in Mplus
full <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4, group = female)
part <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4, group = female, invariance = "ace_sex_abuse")
none <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4, group = female, invariance = "none")
scaling_factor(full)
compare_models(full, part)   # sexual abuse is reported differently by women and men
compare_models(list(full = full, partial = part, none = none))   # each vs. the previous

lm_end()                     # shut Julia down (lm_start() starts a fresh one)
```

Raw survey or Mplus files often code missing values as `-999`; convert
them before fitting (`dat[dat == -999] <- NA`).

The older positional form (`lca(items_df, 3)`,
`r3step(m, covariates_df)`, `bch(m, y_vector)`) still works.

## Tables

`lm_table()` formats results for papers in four formats: `"text"`
(console), `"markdown"` (GitHub), `"latex"` (booktabs) and `"html"`. It
returns the table, and writes it to a file if you give `file`. In R
Markdown and Quarto the table is inserted as it is.

``` r
fits <- lapply(1:5, function(k) lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = k))
names(fits) <- paste0(1:5, "-class")

# class enumeration: K, free parameters, LL, AIC, BIC, saBIC, entropy, smallest class,
# plus LMR / BLRT p-values if you pass them (the lowest information criteria are in bold)
lm_table(fits, lmr  = lapply(fits, function(m) if (m$info$fit$K > 1) lmr(m)),
               blrt = lapply(fits, function(m) if (m$info$fit$K > 1) blrt(m)),
         format = "markdown")
lm_table(fits[[3]], fits[[4]], format = "latex", file = "fit.tex", label = "tab:fit")

# parameters: classes side by side ("est (SE)", stars on testable parameters),
# or one row per parameter; confidence intervals instead of SEs
lm_table(fits[[4]], what = "parameters", format = "latex", file = "lca4.tex")
lm_table(fits[[4]], what = "parameters", layout = "long", ci = TRUE, format = "html")
lm_table(fits[[4]], what = "classes")      # class sizes, average posterior probabilities

# auxiliary models
lm_table(r3step(fits[[4]], aces, c(age, female)), format = "markdown")
lm_table(bch(fits[[4]], aces, depress), bch(fits[[4]], aces, smoker), pairwise = TRUE)
lm_table(dcat(fits[[4]], aces, srh), format = "html", file = "srh.html")
lm_table(compare_models(full, part), format = "latex")
```

Options: `digits`, `title`, `notes`, `stars = c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001)` (or
`FALSE`), `se`, `ci`, `level`, `layout`, `kinds`, `labels`.

### Extending `lm_table()`

`lm_table()` is an S3 generic. A package with its own result class
builds an `lm_tab` (formatted cells, optional panel groups, title,
notes) and renders it with `lm_render()`, which takes care of the four
formats:

``` r
#' @exportS3Method latentmixtures::lm_table
lm_table.my_result <- function(x, ..., format = c("text", "markdown", "latex", "html"),
                               digits = 3, file = NULL, title = NULL, notes = NULL, label = NULL) {
  body <- data.frame(Class = paste("Class", seq_along(x$est)),
                     Effect = paste0(lm_format_num(x$est, digits), lm_stars(x$p)),
                     SE = lm_format_num(x$se, digits), p = lm_format_p(x$p))
  tab <- lm_tab(body, title = title %||% "My estimates", notes = notes)
  lm_render(tab, match.arg(format), file = file, label = label)
}
```

## Plots

Every model and auxiliary result has an `autoplot()` method (ggplot2),
and `plot()` draws the same figure. The functions return ggplot objects,
so titles, scales and themes can be changed with `+`. The default theme
(`lm_theme()`) and the colour-blind-safe Okabe-Ito palette
(`lm_palette()`) are exported for your own figures.

``` r
m <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4)
autoplot(m, error = "ci")            # item-response profiles with 95% CIs
autoplot(m, type = "bars")           # stacked category probabilities per class
autoplot(m, type = "classification") # average posterior probabilities by modal class
autoplot(m, type = "posterior")      # histograms of the assigned-class posteriors
autoplot(m, type = "sizes")          # estimated class proportions and modal counts

# class enumeration: information criteria and entropy against K, LMR / BLRT p-values
lm_fitplot(fits, lmr = lapply(fits, function(m) if (m$info$fit$K > 1) lmr(m)))
```

![](reference/figures/README-lca-profile.png)

LCA item-response profiles

![](reference/figures/README-enumeration.png)

Class enumeration

``` r
p <- lpa(wellbeing, sleep:lifesat, K = 4, variances = "varying")
p_full <- lpa(wellbeing, sleep:lifesat, K = 4, variances = "varying", covariances = "varying")
autoplot(p, standardize = TRUE)      # profile means ± 95% CI, in overall-SD units
autoplot(p, error = "sd")            # means ± within-profile SD
autoplot(p_full, type = "correlation")   # within-profile correlations (covariances != "zero")
```

![](reference/figures/README-lpa-profile.png)

LPA profiles

``` r
t <- lta(substance, waves = list(alc_1:mj_1, alc_2:mj_2, alc_3:mj_3), K = 3)
autoplot(t)                          # LTA transition matrices, one panel per transition
autoplot(t, type = "prevalence")     # class proportions over the waves (geom = "area")
autoplot(t, type = "profile")        # item profiles at every wave (non-invariance)
```

![](reference/figures/README-lta-transitions.png)

LTA transitions

``` r
# growth mixtures: estimated class trajectories, observed posterior-weighted class
# means and a sample of individual trajectories (one panel per process)
g <- growth(depression, dep1:dep5, K = 4, model = "gmm", degree = 2)
autoplot(g, data = depression, spaghetti = 60)
```

![](reference/figures/README-growth.png)

Growth mixture trajectories

Other figures: multigroup models (one panel per group),
`autoplot(m, type = "regression")` for one-step covariates and
`autoplot(r3step(...))` (odds-ratio forest plots), `autoplot(bch(...))`
/ `autoplot(dcat(...))` (class means / probabilities with CIs),
`autoplot(blrt(...))` (bootstrap distribution of the LR statistic) and
`autoplot(compare_models(m1, m2, m3))` (dot plot of the fit indices).
See `?autoplot.latentmix` and the vignettes.

## Julia session

-   `lm_start(threads = "auto")` starts one Julia process, sets
    `JULIA_NUM_THREADS` and loads LatentMixtures.jl once. Later calls
    reuse it. Fitting functions start it automatically, using
    `JULIA_NUM_THREADS` if it is set and `"auto"` otherwise.
-   `lm_status()` reports whether Julia is running and how many threads
    it has.
-   `lm_end()` stops the process. Models fitted before still print
    (their fit statistics are kept in R), but anything that needs Julia
    asks you to refit them.
-   You cannot change the number of threads of a running process. To
    change it, run `lm_end(); lm_start(threads = n)`.
-   `lm_session_id()` increases with each new Julia process. Packages
    that load their own Julia code can check it to know when to reload.

# Package index

## All functions

-   `aces` : Adverse childhood experiences (simulated)

-   `autoplot(<latentmix_bch>)` `autoplot(<latentmix_dcat>)`
    `autoplot(<latentmix_r3step>)` `autoplot(<latentmix_blrt>)`
    `plot(<latentmix_bch>)` `plot(<latentmix_dcat>)`
    `plot(<latentmix_r3step>)` `plot(<latentmix_blrt>)` : Plot
    auxiliary-model results

-   `autoplot(<latentmix>)` `plot(<latentmix>)` : Plot a fitted mixture
    model

-   `bch()` : Continuous distal outcome means by class (BCH; Mplus
    AUXILIARY = y (BCH))

-   `blrt()` : Bootstrap likelihood-ratio test of K-1 against K classes
    (Mplus TECH14)

-   `bvr()` : Bivariate residuals of a latent class model

-   `classification_table()` : Classification diagnostics (Mplus
    CLASSIFICATION QUALITY)

-   `classify()` `posterior()` : Posterior class probabilities and class
    membership

-   `classprobs()` : Estimated class proportions

-   `coeftable()` : Regression coefficients of the one-step latent class
    regression

-   `compare_models()` : Compare nested models with the same number of
    classes

-   `compare_mplus()` : Compare a fit with Mplus

-   `conditionalprobs()` : Within-class distribution in each between
    class (two-level models)

-   `convergence()` `print(<lm_convergence>)` : Check the convergence of
    a fitted mixture model

-   `countparams()` : Count-indicator parameters of a mixture model

-   `dcat()` : Categorical distal outcome by class (Mplus DCAT)

-   `depression` : Adolescent depressive and anxiety symptoms, ages
    12–16 (simulated)

-   `fitstats()` : Fit statistics

-   `fittable()` : Fit statistics of several models (e.g. 1 to 6
    classes)

-   `growth()` : Growth mixture models (LCGA, GMM, parallel processes)

-   `growthparams()` : Growth parameters of LCGA / GMM models

-   `install_julia_packages()` : Install the Julia packages used by
    latentmixtures

-   `itemprobs()` : Item-response probabilities of an LCA

-   `julia_threads()` :

    Set the number of Julia threads (superseded by `lm_start()`)

-   `logLik(<latentmix>)` `nobs(<latentmix>)` `coef(<latentmix>)`
    `predict(<latentmix>)` : Standard methods for fitted latent mixture
    models

-   `latentmixtures` `latentmixtures-package` : latentmixtures: latent
    class, profile, transition and growth mixture models via Julia

-   `lca()` : Latent class analysis

-   `lm_available()` : Is Julia with LatentMixtures.jl available?

-   `lm_fitplot()` `autoplot(<latentmix_comparison>)`
    `autoplot(<latentmix_compare>)` `plot(<latentmix_comparison>)` :
    Plot fit indices for class enumeration or model comparison

-   `lm_format_num()` `lm_format_p()` `lm_stars()` : Format numbers,
    p-values and significance stars for tables

-   `lm_session_id()` : Identifier of the current Julia session

-   `lm_start()` `lm_end()` `lm_status()` `print(<lm_status>)` : Start,
    stop and inspect the Julia session

-   `lm_tab()` `lm_render()` `print(<lm_table_output>)`
    `as.character(<lm_table_output>)` `print(<lm_tab>)` : Build and
    render a table

-   `lm_table()` : Publication tables of models and auxiliary results

-   `lm_theme()` `lm_palette()` : Theme and colour palette of the
    package's plots

-   `lmr()` : Vuong-Lo-Mendell-Rubin test of K-1 against K classes
    (Mplus TECH11)

-   `lpa()` : Latent profile analysis

-   `lrtest()` : Likelihood-ratio test of nested models with the same
    number of classes

-   `lta()` : Latent transition analysis

-   `lta3step()` : ML three-step latent transition analysis (covariates
    and distal outcomes)

-   `mixture()` : Mixture model with mixed indicator types

-   `pairprobs()` : Joint probabilities of locally dependent item pairs

-   `parameters()` : Parameter estimates with robust (Mplus MLR)
    standard errors

-   `print(<latentmix>)` : Print a fitted latent mixture model

-   `print(<latentmix_aux>)` `print(<latentmix_r3step>)`
    `print(<latentmix_bch>)` `print(<latentmix_dcat>)`
    `print(<latentmix_lmr>)` `print(<latentmix_blrt>)`
    `print(<latentmix_compare>)` `print(<latentmix_comparison>)` : Print
    auxiliary-model and test results

-   `profilemeans()` `profilevariances()` `profilecovariances()` :
    Profile means, variances and covariances of an LPA or a continuous
    LTA

-   `r3step()` : Three-step regression of class membership on covariates
    (Mplus R3STEP)

-   `refit_start()` : Refit a model from one of its random starts

-   `scaling_factor()` : MLR scaling correction factor

-   `schools` : Students nested in schools (simulated)

-   `substance` : Adolescent substance use in grades 8, 10 and 12
    (simulated)

-   `summary(<latentmix>)` `print(<summary.latentmix>)` : Summary of a
    fitted model with all parameters

-   `to_mplus()` : Export a fitted model to Mplus

-   `transitions()` : Transition matrices of an LTA

-   `twostep()` : Two-step estimation of covariate effects in a
    two-level latent class model

-   `vcov(<latentmix>)` : Covariance matrix of the parameter estimates

-   `weightdiagnostics()` : Effective number of cases behind each class
    (weight diagnostics)

-   `wellbeing` : Health behaviours and wellbeing (simulated)

-   `wellbeing_panel` : Wellbeing before and during the COVID-19
    pandemic (simulated panel)
